title: The Manor
subtitle: An identity for nourishment and wellbeing
intro: The Manor was a lifestyle store concept planned for Fort Canning Park in Singapore, bringing dining, responsible provisions and events together. I developed its visual identity around a simple idea: appreciating where products come from and the people, skills and resources behind them.
meta: Branding · Visual identity proposal · 2019 · Not launched
brief:
The Manor paired fair and ethical consumption with premium dining and carefully selected products. Its identity needed to communicate that quality while staying warm, honest and straightforward.

The setting and intended audience were important starting points for the brand’s positioning. The design direction brought those ambitions into a coherent visual language, with a sincere voice and an emphasis on the people behind the products.

The identity also needed to connect three experiences: The Tea Room for tea appreciation and vegan dining, The Sundry Lounge for groceries and crafts, and The Attic for events.

process.title: One family, three experiences
process.body: The parent brand and its three sub-brands share a typographic structure. A handwritten “the” sits above the wordmarks, while descriptive taglines explain each offer.
process.caption: The Manor and its three sub-brands, with descriptive taglines.

process.title: Flexible wordmarks
process.body: Versions without taglines accommodate smaller applications and printing methods where fine text would be difficult to reproduce. The proposal also defines clearspace, minimum sizes and approved logo use.
process.caption: Alternative wordmarks without taglines.

process.title: A warm, grounded palette
process.body: Lush Green and Warm Tan form the primary palette. Their lighter tints create room for quieter applications, while navy, burgundy, berry red and brass distinguish product collections.
process.caption: Primary colours and their tints.

process.title: Colour with a practical role
process.body: The secondary colours extend the identity across collateral and provide a way to distinguish products within The Sundry Lounge.
process.caption: Secondary colours for brand collateral and product categories.

delivery: Menus and packaging put the brand’s values into practice visually. Producer stories sit alongside product information, giving the people behind the goods a place in the experience. Minerva Modern and Benton Sans create a shared typographic language, with condensed styles giving product names their own presence.

guidelines.caption: The Tea Room menu, with colour-coded section tabs.
Proposed tea packaging, featuring producer stories alongside product information.
A consistent label system for coffee origins.
Colour variations across food, drinks and home products.

takeawayTitle: A shared identity across different experiences
takeaway:
A brand identity tells a story.
Every visual choice helps communicate what a brand stands for and how it wants people to feel.

Understanding comes before designing.
Exploring a brand’s values, mission and ambitions gives the visual identity a clear purpose.

The story needs to hold together.
From the wordmark to the packaging, each application should feel like part of the same brand.

results.title: One coherent identity across three distinct experiences
items: The Manor and its three sub-brands shared a consistent wordmark structure while retaining clear identities for each offer.
Brand values expressed through the details
Producer stories, materials, colour and typography gave ethical consumption and premium quality a tangible visual expression.
Guidelines, menus and packaging concepts demonstrated how the identity could work across everyday customer touchpoints. The project remained an unlaunched proposal.
